title: @dzup-ui/testing security corpus file
description: One category of hostile inputs and the outcome each sink kind owes them. Schema 1.1.0. Authority: checkCorpusFile() in @dzup-ui/testing/security-corpus, which also enforces what JSON Schema cannot (unique fixture ids); `yarn validate:security-corpus` fails if this schema and that checker ever disagree about a data file. Vocabulary and contribution path: security-corpus/README.md.
$comment: Draft-07 and only the keywords packages/tooling/src/token-checks/json-schema-draft07.ts implements (no minLength, no propertyNames, no $defs): the gate evaluates this file with that evaluator and refuses any keyword it does not know. Non-empty strings are therefore `pattern: \S`.

$schema.description: Editor hint: a path or URL to this file.

schemaVersion.description: x.y.z. The major must be 1; a file with another major is rejected rather than best-effort parsed.

category.description: The class of hostile input. url-scheme: a URL whose scheme decides reference vs execution. markup-injection: a string that is markup. css-injection: a string reaching a CSS value or style attribute. degenerate-input: too long, invisible, or read differently by human and machine. file-metadata: a name, MIME type or size on a user-chosen file. encoded-payload: a value encoded for another system to decode.

sink.description: Where the value lands — the property that decides what safe means. navigation: followed on activation (). subresource: fetched (). html: reaches an HTML parser. markdown: Markdown source whose rendered HTML reaches an HTML parser. mermaid-svg: Mermaid source whose rendered SVG reaches an HTML parser. text: a text node. attribute: an attribute value. style: a CSS declaration. encoded-payload: encoded for another system. file: a user-chosen File.

outcome.description: What must be observably true, strongest first. rejected: never reached the sink. stripped: the dangerous part removed, the remainder kept. escaped: present verbatim as data, built no element/attribute/handler. inert: present verbatim and the sink cannot act on it (rationale required). admitted: reaches the sink live and unchanged because a named policy deliberately admits it — not a neutralization (rationale required, naming the policy).

extensions.description: Consumer-specific data keyed by a reverse-DNS namespace (com.dzup.pro). A reader ignores namespaces it does not know; an extension never changes the meaning of a shared field.

id.description: {category}.{family}.{case}, lowercase kebab segments. Never reused for a different payload.

payload.description: The input verbatim, or with `repeat` the unit it is built from. Always resolve through payloadOf().

outcomes.description: The required outcome per sink kind. A sink absent from the map is one the fixture says nothing about — never 'anything goes'.

not.description: Non-empty: a fixture that names no required outcome asserts only 'does not crash'.

rationale.description: Longer than 80 characters wherever inert or admitted is claimed.
